inputs.text: Photorealistic Thai food photography for a Bangkok restaurant menu: a Thai-style creamy coconut curry, glossy and appetizing, with large visible cooked ingredients on top, served over jasmine rice on the SAME plate with plenty of rice grains exposed along one edge. Overhead close-up of ONE coherent finished Thai-inspired dish in ONE shallow blue-and-white Thai ceramic plate, on a warm teak table with a subtle banana-leaf placemat underneath the plate. The dish contains 6 selected ingredient types: Rice, Egg, Shrimp, Garlic, Mushroom, Coconut milk. All selected ingredients are large, individually recognizable and fully visible INSIDE the same plated dish: Thai jasmine rice with separate elongated grains, delicate grain edges and a light moist sheen; a Thai crispy fried egg with fine lacy golden edges, gently blistered opaque egg white and a rich glossy yellow yolk; cooked pink-orange curled shrimp with distinct segmented flesh, gently seared edges and recognizable tails; small separate peeled garlic cloves, smooth ivory teardrop shapes with pointed tips and subtle golden sear spots, each a single clove rather than a whole garlic head; pan-fried brown mushroom halves with irregular caramelized caps, recognizable stems and fine visible gills on cut sides; smooth silky ivory coconut milk with fine glossy highlights and delicate pale cream swirls. Distribute all selected ingredients visibly across the surface of this ONE cooked dish, integrated naturally with the Thai preparation while keeping every ingredient easy to recognize and uncovered. No isolated piles of ingredient samples, no compartment tray, no Western steak-and-sides plating. Every selected ingredient must be visible, not minced, pureed, buried or dissolved. Use only the selected visible food ingredients; do not add unselected rice, chili, basil, lime or other food garnishes. No separate ingredient bowls, raw ingredient display, collage, grid, labels, writing or hands. The food fills most of the frame. Soft directional window daylight skims across the food, revealing fine natural surface texture and gentle contact shadows. Appetizing realistic cooking detail: subtle irregular browning, moist cut surfaces, delicate crisp edges where appropriate, and small controlled highlights on juices and sauce. Natural variations in size and shape, never identical repeated pieces. Professional close food photograph with rich but believable colors, balanced exposure and clean fine detail. The entire serving and every selected ingredient remain sharply focused and fully inside the frame. Food texture is the main subject; the ceramic rim and background are secondary. Natural photographic texture rather than waxy smooth plastic, illustration or aggressive sharpening.
